draft.headline: Nasdaq futures down 2.59% after tech earnings news; no US data this morning
draft.summary: No US economic data came out this morning, and none is scheduled today. NQ is down 2.59% and sits just above its overnight low. Headlines point to sharp drops in Amazon and Intel after earnings. The mood into the open is negative.
draft.what_it_means: With no data on the calendar, today is about company news. Headlines say Amazon slid 7% and Intel plunged 25% after earnings. One headline calls it a "tech scare trade." Treat these as headlines, not confirmed figures. Big Nasdaq 100 members can move the whole index. A record $6.3 billion Binance crypto hack is also in the news. Oil at $104.24 keeps inflation worries alive, and headlines link high refining profits to the Iran war.
draft.market_reaction: NQ is at 28,797.00, down 2.59%. S&P 500 futures are down 1.10%, so tech is leading the drop. NQ is 33.00 points above its overnight low. It is below yesterday's low and below last week's low of 28,992.75. The 2.59% fall is bigger than NQ's typical full-day range of 1.68%. The VIX fear gauge rose 8.26% to 18.62. Oil rose 2.20%, gold fell 1.63% and the dollar slipped 0.22%.
draft.rates_read: The 2-year yield fell 5.0bp to 4.606%, and the 10-year also fell 5.0bp to 4.939%. Falling yields usually help Nasdaq stocks, yet NQ fell anyway. That suggests rates are not driving today's drop, and company news looks more important. Yields falling while stocks drop can mean money is moving to the safety of bonds, but the facts don't confirm why. The curve (10-year minus 2-year) held at +33bp.

draft.learn: Index weight: the Nasdaq 100 gives bigger companies more weight. A big drop in a giant like Amazon pulls the whole index down more than a drop in a small company would. That's why a few earnings reports can move NQ much more than the S&P 500.
